{{short description|American environmental engineer (born 1951)}}
'''James F. Pankow''' (born 1951) is an American environmental engineer.

Pankow studied chemistry at the [[Binghamton University|State University of New York at Binghamton]] in 1973, and earned a doctorate in engineering from the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1979. He is a professor of chemistry and engineering at [[Portland State University]]. Pankow has been an [[ISI highly cited researcher]] since 2003.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dr. James F. Pankow |url=https://www.pdx.edu/profile/dr-james-f-pankow |accessdate=January 28, 2019 |publisher=Portland State University |archive-date=January 28, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190128030429/https://www.pdx.edu/profile/dr-james-f-pankow |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2009, Pankow was elected a member of the [[United States National Academy of Engineering]] "for  contributions to understanding the chemical thermodynamics of organic particulate matter in urban air and the global atmosphere."<ref>{{cite news |title=Professor James F. Pankow Elected to Prestigious National Academy of Engineering |url=https://www.pdx.edu/clas/professor-james-f-pankow-elected-to-prestigious-national-academy-of-engineering |accessdate=January 28, 2019 |publisher=Portland State University |date=2009 |archive-date=January 28, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190128030418/https://www.pdx.edu/clas/professor-james-f-pankow-elected-to-prestigious-national-academy-of-engineering |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Dr. James F. Pankow |url=https://www.nae.edu/30323.aspx |accessdate=January 28, 2019 |publisher=United States National Academy of Engineering}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 1993, Dr. James F. Pankow received the [[John Wesley Powell Award]] (specifically the National Citizen Achievement Award) from the [[U.S. Geological Survey]] (USGS).<ref>{{cite web |title=Aquatic Chemistry Concepts, Second Edition |url=https://www.routledge.com/Aquatic-Chemistry-Concepts-Second-Edition/Pankow/p/book/9781032337739 |access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref> In 1999, Pankow was co-awarded the [[American Chemical Society (ACS)]] Award for Creative Advances in Environmental Science and Technology in recognition of his pioneering research into how organic pollutants distribute themselves between gas and particulate phases in the atmosphere.<ref>{{cite web |title=ACS Award for Creative Advances in Environmental Science and Technology Recipients |url=https://www.acs.org/funding/awards/acs-award-for-creative-advances-in-environmental-science-and-technology/past-recipients.html#:~:text=2001%20%2D%20Michael%20R. |website=ACS |access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref>
In 2005, he won the Haagen-Smit Prize.<ref>{{cite web |title=Aquatic Chemistry Concepts, Second Edition |url=https://www.routledge.com/Aquatic-Chemistry-Concepts-Second-Edition/Pankow/p/book/9781032337739 |access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref>
